issue.title: Replace flat composition grid with nested gallery regions
issue.description:
Replace the current flat mixed-span preview grid with a deterministic nested layout architecture inspired by the proven structure observed in tweakcn.

Background:
The current <issue id="611f6f6a-dfbd-49ed-9b95-e16f1cc78ee4" href="https://linear.app/emman-systems/issue/PUI-64/adopt-responsive-mixed-span-composition-grid">PUI-64</issue> implementation uses one global CSS Grid for all compositions. Because all cards participate in shared grid rows, a taller card in one column forces the entire row to that height, creating large dead vertical gaps beneath shorter neighboring cards.

Observed issue:

* Productive Week and Account Profile share a row.
* Account Profile is taller.
* Team Access cannot rise underneath Productive Week because the shared CSS Grid row height is controlled by the taller card.
* This produces visually broken empty space even though card heights are individually natural.

Reference lesson from tweakcn:
Inspection of tweakcn's Cards gallery shows that it does not rely on one global mixed-span grid for every composition.
Instead, it uses:

* an outer responsive layout;
* independent vertical regions/stacks;
* nested local grids only where side-by-side compositions are intentional;
* flex-column stacking for vertically independent card flow;
* full-region width for horizontally long compositions;
* breakpoint-specific region proportions.

The goal is to adopt this structural approach, not to copy exact markup/classes.

Owner direction:

* Replace the current one-global-grid composition gallery.
* Use deterministic nested gallery regions/stacks.
* Preserve natural content-driven card heights.
* Allow vertically independent stacking so a tall card in one region does not create dead space in another.
* Use nested grids only where intentional side-by-side grouping is part of the gallery composition.
* Keep the layout predictable, responsive, source-ordered, and accessible.
* Do not use masonry.

1. Gallery ownership model

Revise the layout responsibility model:

Composition:

* owns content and component composition;
* should not need to encode global gallery placement logic.

Gallery layout recipe:

* owns grouping and arrangement of compositions;
* decides which items belong to which visual region;
* decides whether a local region is a vertical stack or a small nested grid.

Local region:

* controls whether its children stack vertically or sit side-by-side;
* can allow a composition to occupy the full width of that region.

This supersedes the assumption that every composition's global width footprint alone is enough to determine layout.

2. Structural direction

Preferred architecture conceptually:

```
Composition gallery
├── Region A
│   ├── composition
│   ├── composition
│   └── composition
└── Region B
    ├── local two-column group
    │   ├── composition
    │   └── composition
    ├── full-region composition
    └── full-region composition
```

The exact API/data structure should fit the existing composition registry and Workbench architecture.

Do not over-generalize into an arbitrary page-layout DSL.

3. Responsive behavior

Wide desktop:

* use two major gallery regions with intentionally chosen proportions;
* exact proportions may be determined from current visual fit rather than copied blindly from tweakcn;
* regions stack their own children independently;
* local nested grids may display intentional side-by-side cards.

Medium:

* preserve region separation where space permits;
* nested local groups may collapse from two columns to one where required.

Small/mobile:

* collapse to a single readable source-ordered flow;
* no horizontal overflow;
* no hidden/reordered interactive content.

The worker should preserve logical DOM/focus order and avoid visual reordering that conflicts with keyboard/accessibility order.

4. Height behavior

* Card height remains natural/content-driven.
* No forced equal-height rows.
* No forced square aspect ratio.
* A taller card in one region must not hold down unrelated cards in another region.
* Vertically stacked cards should pack immediately after the preceding card in their own region.

5. Remove global row coupling

The accepted fix must eliminate the current shared-row behavior where unrelated compositions create dead vertical space.

The worker should explicitly reproduce and verify the current failure case before changing the layout, then prove the dead-gap condition is removed afterward.

6. Relationship to <issue id="611f6f6a-dfbd-49ed-9b95-e16f1cc78ee4" href="https://linear.app/emman-systems/issue/PUI-64/adopt-responsive-mixed-span-composition-grid">PUI-64</issue>

<issue id="611f6f6a-dfbd-49ed-9b95-e16f1cc78ee4" href="https://linear.app/emman-systems/issue/PUI-64/adopt-responsive-mixed-span-composition-grid">PUI-64</issue> introduced:

* responsive mixed-width composition intent;
* natural card heights;
* representative wide compositions.

Retain the useful visual goals from <issue id="611f6f6a-dfbd-49ed-9b95-e16f1cc78ee4" href="https://linear.app/emman-systems/issue/PUI-64/adopt-responsive-mixed-span-composition-grid">PUI-64</issue>, but replace the flat global-grid implementation that caused row-height coupling.

Do not preserve architecture merely for backward compatibility if it directly causes the visual defect.

If `PreviewLayout = "default" | "wide"` is no longer the right abstraction after this change:

* simplify, adapt, or remove it;
* document the new ownership model;
* avoid keeping redundant layout metadata.

7. Initial layout

Use the current Cards gallery as the implementation target.

The Lead/worker should determine a coherent initial region grouping from the existing eight compositions, guided by:

* visual balance;
* natural card height;
* chart/table width needs;
* semantic grouping where useful;
* responsive behavior.

The goal is not exact parity with tweakcn's card content, only the same stronger structural layout principle.

8. Boundaries

* No masonry engine.
* No CSS masonry dependency on experimental browser behavior.
* No arbitrary drag/drop placement.
* No user-facing layout editor.
* No generic layout DSL.
* No absolute positioning.
* No component/resource-level hardcoding of global gallery placement.
* Do not change composition content unless necessary for layout compatibility.
* Preserve shadcn-first component architecture.

Scope:

* Workbench Cards gallery layout container.
* Composition gallery metadata/recipe if required.
* Removal/refactor of current flat-grid span logic.
* Responsive nested region/group styles.
* Tests and browser verification.
* Documentation of the final layout ownership model.

Acceptance:

* The current dead-space failure caused by shared global grid rows is eliminated.
* Tall cards in one region no longer force vertical gaps in another region.
* Natural card heights are preserved.
* Gallery uses deterministic nested regions/stacks rather than masonry.
* Side-by-side cards appear only in intentional local nested grids.
* Horizontally long compositions can occupy the full width of their local region.
* Wide desktop layout feels balanced and supports long rectangular compositions.
* Medium and small breakpoints collapse coherently.
* No horizontal overflow is introduced.
* DOM, reading, keyboard, and focus order remain coherent.
* No regression to composition interactions or accessibility.
* Worker documents the final layout structure, breakpoint behavior, and whether old `PreviewLayout` metadata was retained, adapted, or removed.
